119	**[ARTICLE II --- PROPERTY DESCRIPTION]{.underline}**
120	
121	**Section 2.1 --- Sale of Property**
122	
123	Subject to the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement, Seller agrees to sell, convey, transfer, and assign to Buyer, and Buyer agrees to purchase and acquire from Seller, all of Seller\'s right, title, and interest in and to the following (collectively, the \"**Property**\"):
124	
125	> \(a\) **The Land.** The Land, as more particularly described in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference, consisting of approximately 22.8 acres located at 4700 Briarwood Commons Drive, Charlotte, NC 28270, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, identified as Tax Parcel ID 18904327;
126	>
127	> \(b\) **The Improvements.** All buildings, structures, fixtures, and improvements located on the Land, including fourteen (14) garden-style residential buildings containing a total of three hundred twelve (312) residential apartment units, together with all amenity facilities including a swimming pool, fitness center, dog park, business center, package lockers, and related clubhouse and leasing office space, and four hundred sixty-eight (468) surface parking spaces;
128	>
129	> \(c\) **Personal Property.** All Personal Property owned by Seller and located on or used in connection with the ownership, operation, or maintenance of the Property, including all furniture, fixtures, equipment, appliances, tools, supplies, and other items of tangible personal property;
130	>
131	> \(d\) **Leases.** All Leases, including, without limitation, all residential leases and the Commercial Lease with Little Oaks Learning Center, together with all security deposits, prepaid rents, and other amounts held by Seller under such Leases;
132	>
133	> \(e\) **Intangible Property.** All Intangible Property, including, without limitation, all permits, licenses, approvals, entitlements, warranties, guaranties, trade names (including the name \"The Ellington at Briarwood\"), telephone numbers, website addresses, plans, specifications, drawings, utility deposits, books and records, and all other intangible rights relating to the ownership, operation, or maintenance of the Property; and
134	>
135	> \(f\) **Appurtenances.** All easements, rights-of-way, privileges, rights of ingress and egress, hereditaments, and appurtenances belonging to or inuring to the benefit of the Land or the Improvements, including, without limitation, any and all rights of Seller in and to any strips or gores of land adjacent to the Land and any rights of Seller in and to any public or private streets, roads, or alleys adjacent to or abutting the Land.
136	
137	**Section 2.2 --- Condition of Property**
138	
139	Buyer acknowledges and agrees that, except as expressly set forth in Seller\'s representations and warranties in Article VIII and Seller\'s covenants in Article VII, Buyer will purchase the Property in its \"**AS-IS, WHERE-IS, WITH ALL FAULTS**\" condition as of the Closing Date. Buyer acknowledges that it will have had the opportunity, during the Due Diligence Period, to conduct such inspections, investigations, tests, studies, and analyses of the Property as Buyer deems appropriate, including, without limitation, physical inspections, environmental assessments, engineering studies, review of financial records, review of Leases, and such other due diligence as Buyer determines to be necessary or advisable.
140	
141	Buyer further acknowledges that, except as expressly set forth in Article VIII of this Agreement, Seller has not made and does not make any representations or warranties of any kind, whether express or implied, with respect to the Property, including, without limitation, any representations or warranties regarding the physical condition of the Property, the environmental condition of the Property, the fitness of the Property for any particular purpose, the compliance of the Property with applicable laws, the accuracy of any financial information or projections provided to Buyer, or any other matter relating to the Property.
142	
143	**Notwithstanding the foregoing**, the \"as-is, where-is, with all faults\" provisions of this Section 2.2 shall not be deemed or construed to limit, modify, negate, or otherwise diminish: (a) any of Seller\'s representations and warranties expressly set forth in Article VIII of this Agreement; (b) any of Seller\'s covenants or obligations expressly set forth in Article VII of this Agreement; (c) Seller\'s indemnification obligations under Article XV of this Agreement; or (d) any other express obligation or undertaking of Seller under this Agreement. The Parties acknowledge and agree that the as-is provisions of this Section 2.2 are intended to complement and operate in conjunction with, and not in derogation of, Seller\'s express representations, warranties, covenants, and obligations under this Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this Section 2.2 and the provisions of Article VIII, Article VII, or Article XV, the provisions of Article VIII, Article VII, or Article XV, as applicable, shall control.
144	
145	**[ARTICLE III --- PURCHASE PRICE AND EARNEST MONEY]{.underline}**
146	
147	**Section 3.1 --- Purchase Price**
148	
149	The total purchase price for the Property shall be Fifty-Seven Million Two Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars (\$57,200,000) (the \"**Purchase Price**\"), payable by Buyer to Seller as follows:
150	
151	> \(a\) **Initial Deposit.** Within three (3) business days after the Effective Date (i.e., on or before November 7, 2024), Buyer shall deposit with Escrow Agent the sum of Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars (\$750,000) (the \"**Initial Deposit**\") by wire transfer of immediately available funds.
152	>
153	> \(b\) **Additional Deposit.** Upon the expiration of the Due Diligence Period (i.e., on or before December 4, 2024), provided Buyer has not elected to terminate this Agreement pursuant to Section 5.4, Buyer shall deposit with Escrow Agent an additional sum of Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars (\$750,000) (the \"**Additional Deposit**\") by wire transfer of immediately available funds.
154	>
155	> \(c\) **Balance of Purchase Price.** The balance of the Purchase Price, after application of the Earnest Money Deposit and subject to prorations and adjustments as set forth in Article XI, shall be paid by Buyer to Seller (or as otherwise directed by Seller) at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by Seller or Escrow Agent in writing not fewer than two (2) business days prior to the Closing Date.
156	
157	**Section 3.2 --- Earnest Money Deposit**
158	
159	The Initial Deposit and the Additional Deposit shall collectively constitute the \"**Earnest Money Deposit**,\" totaling One Million Five Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars (\$1,500,000) in the aggregate. The Escrow Agent shall hold the Earnest Money Deposit in a federally insured, interest-bearing account at a financial institution mutually agreed upon by the Parties. All interest accruing on the Earnest Money Deposit shall accrue for the benefit of, and shall be paid to, the Party ultimately entitled to receive the Earnest Money Deposit pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. The Escrow Agent shall not commingle the Earnest Money Deposit with any other funds and shall not disburse the Earnest Money Deposit except in accordance with joint written instructions signed by both Buyer and Seller or in accordance with the express terms of this Agreement. The tax identification number of Buyer shall be used for all interest reporting purposes.
160	
161	**Section 3.3 --- Refundability of Earnest Money Deposit**
162	
163	> \(a\) **During Due Diligence Period.** The Earnest Money Deposit (including the Initial Deposit) shall be fully refundable to Buyer if Buyer terminates this Agreement during the Due Diligence Period for any reason or no reason whatsoever pursuant to Section 5.4 of this Agreement. Upon any such termination, Escrow Agent shall promptly return the Earnest Money Deposit (together with all accrued interest thereon) to Buyer within three (3) business days after receipt of Buyer\'s written notice of termination.
164	>
165	> \(b\) **After Due Diligence Period.** Following the expiration of the Due Diligence Period, the Earnest Money Deposit shall be refundable to Buyer only in the event of: (i) a default by Seller under this Agreement that is not cured within the applicable cure period set forth in Section 13.1; (ii) a failure of any condition to Buyer\'s obligation to close under Section 9.2; (iii) a termination right exercised by Buyer under Article XII (Casualty or Condemnation); or (iv) a termination right exercised by Buyer under Article VI (Title). In any such event, Escrow Agent shall promptly return the Earnest Money Deposit (together with all accrued interest thereon) to Buyer within three (3) business days after receipt of written notice or documentation evidencing Buyer\'s right to such refund.
166	>
167	> The Earnest Money Deposit shall become non-refundable only upon Buyer\'s default under this Agreement after the expiration of the Due Diligence Period. For the avoidance of doubt, the mere expiration of the Due Diligence Period shall not, in and of itself, render the Earnest Money Deposit non-refundable if Buyer retains an independent right to terminate this Agreement and receive a return of the Earnest Money Deposit under the express provisions of Sections 5.3, 6.3, 9.2, 12.1, or 12.2 of this Agreement.
168	>
169	> \(c\) **Failure to Deposit.** If Buyer fails to timely deposit the Initial Deposit or the Additional Deposit in accordance with Section 3.1, Seller may terminate this Agreement upon written notice to Buyer delivered within five (5) business days after the applicable deposit deadline, and upon such termination, neither Party shall have any further obligations hereunder except for those obligations that expressly survive termination. If Seller does not deliver such termination notice within such five (5) business day period, Seller shall be deemed to have waived such failure, and Buyer shall have an additional three (3) business days to make the required deposit.
170	
171	**Section 3.4 --- Independent Consideration**
172	
173	Upon execution of this Agreement, Buyer shall pay to Seller the sum of One Hundred and No/100 Dollars (\$100.00) as independent consideration (the \"**Independent Consideration**\") for Seller\'s execution and delivery of this Agreement and the grant to Buyer of the rights set forth herein, including the Due Diligence Period. The Independent Consideration is non-refundable under all circumstances and shall be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing.
174	
175	**[ARTICLE IV --- CLOSING]{.underline}**
176	
177	**Section 4.1 --- Closing Date**
178	
179	The Closing shall occur on January 3, 2025, which is sixty (60) calendar days from the Effective Date, or such earlier date as may be mutually agreed upon by the Parties in writing (the \"**Closing Date**\"), subject to extension as provided in Section 4.4. Time is of the essence with respect to the Closing Date, as the same may be extended in accordance with this Agreement.
180	
181	**Section 4.2 --- Place of Closing**
182	
183	The Closing shall be conducted through escrow at the offices of Trident Title Services LLC, 227 West Trade Street, Suite 500, Charlotte, NC 28202, or by mail-away closing as mutually agreed upon by the Parties. Each Party shall deliver all required Closing documents to Escrow Agent in sufficient time to permit Closing on the Closing Date.
184	
185	**Section 4.3 --- Closing Costs**
186	
187	The costs and expenses of the Closing shall be allocated between the Parties as follows:
188	
189	> \(a\) **Seller shall pay:** (i) all North Carolina excise tax (revenue stamps) imposed on the deed; (ii) Seller\'s attorneys\' fees and costs; (iii) the cost of releasing or satisfying any existing deeds of trust, mortgages, liens, or other monetary encumbrances affecting the Property; (iv) one-half (1/2) of any escrow fees charged by the Escrow Agent; and (v) all costs associated with Seller\'s title curative work, if any.
190	>
191	> \(b\) **Buyer shall pay:** (i) the premium for the ALTA Owner\'s Policy of Title Insurance; (ii) the cost of any lender\'s title insurance policy required by Buyer\'s Lender; (iii) Buyer\'s attorneys\' fees and costs; (iv) one-half (1/2) of any escrow fees charged by the Escrow Agent; (v) all survey costs; (vi) all recording fees for the deed, deed of trust, and any other loan documents; and (vii) all costs, fees, and expenses related to Buyer\'s financing, including appraisal fees, loan origination fees, and lender\'s counsel fees.
192	>
193	> \(c\) **Each Party** shall bear its own attorneys\' fees and expenses in connection with the negotiation, preparation, and execution of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated herein, except as otherwise expressly provided in Section 16.9.
194	
195	**Section 4.4 --- Extension of Closing Date**
196	
197	Buyer shall have the right to extend the Closing Date for up to two (2) consecutive periods of fifteen (15) calendar days each (each, an \"**Extension Period**\"). The first Extension Period shall extend the Closing Date to January 18, 2025, and the second Extension Period shall extend the Closing Date to February 2, 2025.
198	
199	To exercise each extension, Buyer shall: (a) deliver written notice of such extension to Seller and Escrow Agent at least five (5) business days prior to the then-applicable Closing Date; and (b) pay to Seller (not to Escrow Agent) a non-refundable extension fee in the amount of One Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars (\$100,000) per extension (each, an \"**Extension Fee**\"). Each Extension Fee shall be non-refundable under all circumstances but shall be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing. If Closing does not occur for any reason (other than by reason of Seller\'s default), the Extension Fee(s) shall be retained by Seller and shall not be returned to Buyer. If the Closing does not occur by reason of Seller\'s default, the Extension Fee(s) paid by Buyer shall be returned to Buyer.
200	
201	**[ARTICLE V --- DUE DILIGENCE AND CONTINGENCIES]{.underline}**
202	
203	**Section 5.1 --- Due Diligence Period**
204	
205	Buyer shall have a period of thirty (30) calendar days from the Effective Date (the \"**Due Diligence Period**\"), expiring at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 4, 2024, to conduct Buyer\'s due diligence investigations and inspections of the Property. During the Due Diligence Period, Buyer may investigate all aspects of the Property that Buyer deems relevant, including, without limitation, the physical condition, environmental condition, structural integrity, compliance with applicable laws, financial performance, tenant matters, title and survey matters, and any other matters Buyer considers material to its decision to acquire the Property.
206	
207	During the Due Diligence Period, Buyer and its agents, consultants, contractors, engineers, surveyors, and other representatives (collectively, \"**Buyer\'s Representatives**\") shall have reasonable access to the Property upon at least twenty-four (24) hours\' prior written or email notice to Seller (or Seller\'s property manager), during normal business hours (8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays), to conduct physical inspections, environmental assessments (including Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments), engineering studies, survey work, geotechnical testing, roof inspections, and such other investigations, tests, and studies as Buyer deems necessary or advisable. Buyer shall have the right to enter occupied units with reasonable advance notice to the affected tenants, coordinated through Seller\'s property manager. Buyer shall not perform any invasive testing (including, without limitation, drilling, boring, or sampling of soil or groundwater) without Seller\'s prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.
208	
209	As a condition to Buyer\'s access to the Property, Buyer shall maintain, or cause Buyer\'s Representatives to maintain, commercial general liability insurance with coverage limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) in the aggregate, naming Seller as an additional insured, and shall provide Seller with evidence of such insurance prior to Buyer\'s first entry upon the Property. Buyer shall repair any physical damage to the Property caused by Buyer\'s inspections and shall restore the Property to substantially the same condition as existed prior to such inspections. Buyer shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Seller from and against any and all claims, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or resulting from the activities of Buyer or Buyer\'s Representatives on the Property during the Due Diligence Period, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Seller or the mere discovery of pre-existing conditions. The indemnification obligations of this Section 5.1 shall survive any termination of this Agreement and shall survive Closing.
210	
211	**Section 5.2 --- Seller\'s Due Diligence Deliveries**
212	
213	Within five (5) business days after the Effective Date (i.e., on or before November 11, 2024), Seller shall deliver to Buyer, or make available to Buyer through an electronic data room or other means of access reasonably acceptable to Buyer, true, correct, and complete copies of the following documents and information to the extent in Seller\'s possession or reasonable control:
214	
215	> \(a\) All Leases, including the Commercial Lease with Little Oaks Learning Center, together with all amendments, modifications, supplements, and guaranties related thereto;
216	>
217	> \(b\) A current rent roll as of October 1, 2024, showing the occupancy status of all units (reflecting 292 of 312 units occupied, or approximately 93.6% occupancy), tenant names, unit numbers, lease commencement and expiration dates, monthly rental amounts, security deposit amounts, outstanding balances, and concessions;
218	>
219	> \(c\) Trailing twelve-month (T-12) operating statements for the Property for the period October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2024, including a detailed income and expense statement, capital expenditure summary, and any available year-end financial statements for prior fiscal years;
220	>
221	> \(d\) All service contracts, management agreements, and vendor agreements currently in effect with respect to the Property, including landscaping, pest control, trash removal, elevator maintenance, HVAC maintenance, and any other vendor arrangements;
222	>
223	> \(e\) Real property tax bills for the current and two (2) prior tax years as assessed by Mecklenburg County, together with any pending tax appeals or protests;
224	>
225	> \(f\) Current and prior insurance policies covering the Property, together with a loss history and claims summary for the prior three (3) years;
226	>
227	> \(g\) All environmental reports, including Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments, asbestos surveys, lead-based paint assessments, mold reports, and any correspondence with governmental agencies relating to environmental matters;
228	>
229	> \(h\) All existing surveys, site plans, as-built drawings, and architectural plans relating to the Property;
230	>
231	> \(i\) Capital expenditure records, including detailed documentation of the renovation of 104 units completed between 2019 and 2021, together with contractor invoices, scope of work descriptions, and any related warranties;
232	>
233	> \(j\) Building permits, certificates of occupancy, temporary certificates of occupancy, and any notices, orders, or correspondence received from governmental authorities relating to the Property;
234	>
235	> \(k\) A summary of any pending or threatened litigation, claims, or governmental proceedings affecting the Property or Seller;
236	>
237	> \(l\) Any homeowners\' association, property owners\' association, or master association documents, if applicable, including declarations, bylaws, budgets, and assessments;
238	>
239	> \(m\) Utility bills for the prior twenty-four (24) months, including water, sewer, electric, gas, and trash/recycling;
240	>
241	> \(n\) A complete inventory of all Personal Property located at the Property.
242	
243	Seller\'s delivery of the foregoing documents shall not be deemed to constitute a representation or warranty as to the accuracy or completeness of the information contained therein, except to the extent expressly provided in Article VIII of this Agreement.
244	
245	**Section 5.3 --- Financing Contingency**
246	
247	> \(a\) **Financing Contingency.** Buyer\'s obligation to consummate the Closing is expressly contingent upon Buyer obtaining a binding written commitment for acquisition financing from Buyer\'s Lender or another institutional lender, on terms and conditions reasonably acceptable to Buyer in Buyer\'s sole but good faith discretion (the \"**Financing Contingency**\"). Buyer shall use diligent and good faith efforts to obtain such financing commitment, including submitting a complete loan application to Buyer\'s Lender within fifteen (15) business days after the Effective Date, responding promptly to all lender requests for information, and cooperating fully with Buyer\'s Lender in connection with the underwriting process.
248	>
249	> \(b\) **Financing Contingency Period.** The Financing Contingency shall expire at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 19, 2024, which is forty-five (45) calendar days from the Effective Date (the \"**Financing Contingency Period**\").
250	>
251	> \(c\) **Termination Right.** If Buyer, despite Buyer\'s diligent and good faith efforts, is unable to obtain a financing commitment reasonably satisfactory to Buyer on or before the expiration of the Financing Contingency Period, Buyer may terminate this Agreement by delivering written notice of termination to Seller and Escrow Agent on or before the expiration of the Financing Contingency Period. Upon such termination, the Earnest Money Deposit (together with all accrued interest thereon) shall be returned to Buyer in full within three (3) business days, and neither Party shall have any further obligations under this Agreement except for those obligations that expressly survive termination. In connection with any such termination notice, Buyer shall provide to Seller reasonable evidence that Buyer diligently pursued financing in good faith, which may include a written declination letter from Buyer\'s Lender or a summary of Buyer\'s financing efforts, provided that Buyer shall not be required to disclose proprietary financial information of Buyer or its principals.
252	>
253	> \(d\) **Deemed Waiver.** If Buyer fails to timely deliver a written termination notice to Seller under this Section 5.3 on or before the expiration of the Financing Contingency Period, the Financing Contingency shall be deemed waived, and Buyer\'s obligation to close hereunder shall be unconditional with respect to Buyer\'s ability to obtain acquisition financing.
254	>
255	> \(e\) **Status Updates.** Buyer shall keep Seller reasonably informed of the status of Buyer\'s financing efforts, including providing updates upon Seller\'s reasonable request (but not more frequently than once per week), provided that Buyer shall not be required to disclose the specific financial terms, interest rates, or other proprietary provisions of any loan commitment or term sheet. Buyer shall promptly notify Seller upon receipt of a binding financing commitment.

**Section 16.5 --- Waiver**

No waiver of any provision of this Agreement, or any right or remedy hereunder, shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument signed by the Party against whom enforcement of such waiver is sought. No single or partial exercise of any right or remedy, and no single waiver of any provision, shall be deemed a continuing waiver of such provision or a waiver of any other provision. The failure of either Party to enforce any provision of this Agreement shall not constitute a waiver of such Party\'s right to enforce such provision or any other provision in the future.

**Section 16.6 --- Counterparts**

This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of this Agreement by electronic mail (including PDF) or other electronic transmission shall be deemed to be, and shall have the same force and effect as, delivery of an original executed counterpart.

**Section 16.7 --- Severability**

If any provision of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal, and enforceable, and the validity, legality, and enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall not be affected or impaired thereby.

**Section 16.8 --- Successors and Assigns**

This Agreement shall be binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of the Parties hereto and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, legal representatives, successors, and permitted assigns.

**Section 16.9 --- Attorneys\' Fees**

In any action, suit, or proceeding brought to enforce any provision of this Agreement, to interpret this Agreement, or arising out of or relating to a breach of this Agreement, the prevailing Party shall be entitled to recover from the non-prevailing Party its reasonable attorneys\' fees, court costs, and expenses of litigation, in addition to any other relief to which such prevailing Party may be entitled.

**Section 16.10 --- Confidentiality**

The Parties shall keep confidential the terms, conditions, and provisions of this Agreement and shall not disclose the same to any third party, except: (a) to their respective legal counsel, accountants, financial advisors, lenders, investors, and other professional advisors who have a need to know such information in connection with the transaction contemplated hereby and who agree to maintain the confidentiality thereof; (b) as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or court order; (c) as may be required in connection with any legal proceeding to enforce the terms of this Agreement; or (d) as otherwise mutually agreed in writing by the Parties. This confidentiality obligation shall survive any termination of this Agreement for a period of two (2) years.

**Section 16.11 --- Time of the Essence**

Time is of the essence with respect to all dates, deadlines, and time periods set forth in this Agreement. If any deadline or time period expires on a day that is not a business day, such deadline or time period shall be extended to the next business day.

**Section 16.12 --- Further Assurances**

Each Party shall, from time to time after the Closing, upon the reasonable request of the other Party, execute, acknowledge, and deliver, or cause to be executed, acknowledged, and delivered, such additional documents, instruments, conveyances, and assurances as may be reasonably required to carry out the intent and purposes of this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby.

**Section 16.13 --- No Third-Party Beneficiaries**

This Agreement is made solely for the benefit of the Parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any other person or entity any legal or equitable right, benefit, remedy, or claim under or by reason of this Agreement.

**Section 16.14 --- Construction**

This Agreement has been negotiated at arm\'s length between the Parties, each of which has been represented by legal counsel of its own choosing. This Agreement shall not be construed more strictly against one Party than against the other by virtue of the fact that it may have been prepared or drafted primarily by counsel for one of the Parties. All headings and captions in this Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not be used in the interpretation or construction of this Agreement.

**Section 16.15 --- Dispute Resolution**

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or validity thereof, that cannot be resolved by good faith negotiation between the Parties within thirty (30) days after written notice of such dispute, shall be submitted to final and binding arbitration in Charlotte, North Carolina, administered by the American Arbitration Association in accordance with its Commercial Arbitration Rules then in effect. The arbitration shall be conducted by a single arbitrator who shall be a licensed attorney with at least ten (10) years of experience in commercial real estate transactions. The arbitrator\'s award shall be final and binding on both Parties, and judgment upon the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. The Parties agree that the arbitrator shall have the authority to award reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs to the prevailing Party in accordance with Section 16.9. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo pending arbitration.

**Section 16.16 --- Escrow Provisions**

> \(a\) **Stakeholder.** The Escrow Agent acts solely as a stakeholder and depository with respect to the Earnest Money Deposit and shall have no liability to any Party for any action or omission taken in good faith, except for the Escrow Agent\'s own willful misconduct or gross negligence.
>
> \(b\) **Resignation.** The Escrow Agent may resign as escrow agent at any time upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the Parties. Upon such resignation, the Escrow Agent shall deliver the Earnest Money Deposit to a successor escrow agent mutually designated by the Parties, or, if the Parties cannot agree upon a successor within such thirty (30) day period, to a court of competent jurisdiction.
>

st = doc.styles['Normal']

def rich(p, text, size=None):
    # **bold** markup
    parts = text.split('**')
    for i,pt in enumerate(parts):
        if not pt: continue
        r = p.add_run(pt); r.bold = (i%2==1)
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p

def para(text, bold=False, italic=False, align=None, size=None, after=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    if bold or italic:
        r = p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.italic=italic

    if align=='c': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    if align=='j': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    if after is not None: p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    return p

doc.add_heading('IV. Prioritized Issues List', level=1)
para('Priority key. **Tier 1 (Critical):** deal-breakers, or IC authorization required; reject. **Tier 2 (High):** material economic or risk shift; insist on our form or a close variant. **Tier 3 (Moderate):** important but negotiable or diligence-driven. **Tier 4 (Clean-up):** drafting and conforming. \"T\" = tracked change; \"U\" = untracked departure from our form. Form § references are to our October 21 form; \"Mkp §\" references are to Seller\\'s markup.', align='j', size=10)
H = ['#','Issue (Form § / Mkp §)','What Seller did','Why it matters to Buyer','Recommended response']
W = [0.3,1.15,1.75,1.75,1.75]

doc.add_heading('Tier 1: Critical (reject; IC authorization required to concede)', level=2)
table(H,[
['1','**Financing contingency**\nForm §§5.3, 9.2; definitions\nMkp §§1.1, 5.3, 8.1(e), 3.3','T: deleted the definition, §5.3 and condition 8.1(e). Inserted \"Waiver of Financing Contingency\": Buyer must close \"regardless of whether Buyer has obtained a loan commitment\"; unavailable financing \"shall not excuse Buyer\\'s performance.\" Mkp §3.3 also says financing failure does not support a refund.','Palisade debt of $37,180,000 (65% LTV) is still subject to appraisal (Aldersgate), Phase I and the property condition assessment. A low appraisal cuts loan proceeds dollar-for-dollar at 65% of appraised value. Fund III is not authorized to close all-cash. Combined with Issues 2–3, a lender decline becomes a $1.5M loss at minimum and a specific-performance or damages claim at worst.','**Reject.** Restore Form §5.3 (45 days to Dec 19, 2024 or reset date; good-faith efforts; full refund; deemed waiver; weekly status updates) and condition §9.2. Our form already offers Seller real protections (deemed waiver; evidence of efforts; loan application within 15 business days). Fallback, **only with IC approval**: shorten modestly (e.g., 40 days), tie it to the Palisade timetable, and give Seller a right to receive the declination letter.'],
['2','**Earnest Money refundability**\nForm §3.3(a)–(b), §9.2 final paragraph\nMkp §3.3','T: entire $1.5M deposit becomes non-refundable at due-diligence expiry \"except in the event of a default by Seller.\" Refunds for failure of conditions survive only for conditions \"expressly set forth in Section 8.1.\" U: deleted our §9.2 paragraph giving Buyer a termination-and-refund right when a condition fails, so even §8.1 failures have no express refund mechanism. Title, casualty and condemnation refunds survive only in their own sections.','Directly contrary to IC §5.1 (\"any provision making the deposit hard . . . irrespective of the reason for non-closing . . . would materially alter the risk profile\"). With due diligence at 21 days, $1.5M goes hard on Nov 25, 2024, 24 days before our financing deadline would have run.','**Reject.** Restore Form §3.3(b) refund events (Seller default; failure of a §9.2 condition; casualty or condemnation; title; financing under §5.3) and the clarifying sentence that expiry of due diligence alone does not make the deposit hard. Restore the §9.2 termination/refund paragraph.'],
['3','**Buyer default remedies / liquidated damages**\nForm §13.2\nMkp §§12.1, 12.3','T: liquidated damages are no longer Seller\\'s sole remedy. Seller \"reserves the right to pursue any and all other remedies . . . including . . . actual damages, specific performance, and consequential damages.\" The deposit becomes a \"minimum, and not a maximum.\" §12.3 consequential-damages waiver made one-way (protects Seller only). U: no notice-and-cure period for Buyer default (Form: 10 business days); the waiver of claims against Buyer\\'s affiliates and members is deleted; the Seller-initials block is deleted.','Removes the cap the IC relied on (IC §5.7: \"$1,500,000 represents Buyer\\'s maximum at-risk capital\"). Exposes Fund III to a suit to compel a $57.2M all-cash closing and to consequential damages. Calling the deposit a \"minimum\" while keeping \"liquidated damages\" is internally inconsistent and invites litigation over whether the clause is an enforceable liquidated-damages provision or an unenforceable penalty. That uncertainty cuts against both sides.','**Reject.** Restore Form §13.2 in full: liquidated damages as sole and exclusive remedy, waiver of specific performance and actual/consequential damages, protection of non-recourse parties, 10-business-day cure, initials. Restore mutual consequential-damages waiver (excluding the carve-outs in Form §13.2(i)–(iv)).'],
['4','**Due Diligence Period**\nForm §§1 (def.), 5.1\nMkp §§1.1, 5.1, 3.2','T: 30 to 21 calendar days, so expiry moves from Wed. Dec 4 to Mon. Nov 25, 2024 (Thanksgiving week). The Additional Deposit is accelerated to the same date. U: Buyer\\'s right to enter occupied units (Form §5.1) and the invasive-testing consent standard (\"not unreasonably withheld\") are deleted.','Scope is 312 units in 14 buildings; Phase I (and possible Phase II); property condition assessment; roof and structure; residential and commercial lease audit; T-12 verification ($3,417,600 NOI); zoning; title and survey. Unit-level inspection of the 208 unrenovated units is the core of the value-add underwriting (renovation budget; $295/month premium). Seller deliveries are not due until 5 business days after signing, so 21 days leaves about 2 working weeks.','**Reject** (IC 1(a)). Keep 30 days. Add that if Seller\\'s §5.2 deliveries are late, the period extends day-for-day. Restore occupied-unit access through the property manager and the invasive-testing consent standard.'],
['5','**Seller representations: knowledge, scope, survival, cap, waiver**\nForm §§1 (\"Seller\\'s Knowledge\"), 2.2, 8.1–8.3\nMkp §§1.1, 6.1, 6.2, 6.4','T: knowledge narrowed to \"actual knowledge of Jonathan Aldecott . . . without any duty of investigation or inquiry,\" and repeated in §6.1(d), (f), (g), (h). Survival cut from 12 to 3 months (to Apr. 3, 2025). New $500,000 aggregate cap. No consequential damages. New §6.4 non-reliance and waiver of \"any claim . . . for matters that could have been discovered\" in due diligence; the knowledge qualifier applies \"notwithstanding any other provision.\"\nU: deleted Form §8.3 (no cap) and the Form §2.2 paragraph protecting reps from the as-is clause. Narrowed or deleted reps: (a) member approval by Aldecott Family Holdings LP; (c) conveyance of good and marketable title; (d) lease copies true and complete, no other occupancy agreements, security deposits, notices to vacate; (g) USTs, NPL listing, pending environmental claims; (h) ADA/FHA and written violation notices; (j) special assessments; (l) **no options/ROFR (deleted)**; (m) pending insurance claims; (o) **renovation code compliance, permits and licensed contractors (deleted)**; Form §5.2 statement that deliveries are true, correct and complete.','The knowledge person is a passive manager whose counsel says the family has \"limited direct involvement\" and relies on a third-party manager, so the reps would cover almost nothing. The discoverability waiver lets Seller defend nearly any claim by arguing Buyer\\'s consultants could have found the problem. Three months does not cover even one full post-closing operating quarter, tax re-billing, or year-end reconciliation. A $500,000 cap is 0.87% of price. The deleted renovation rep goes to the heart of the value-add thesis (104 units renovated 2019–2021; quality and permitting of that work drives the projected rent premium). IC §8 lists \"significant reduction in the survival period or scope\" as requiring IC authorization.','**Reject.** Restore the Form knowledge definition: actual knowledge of Mr. Aldecott after reasonable inquiry of the property manager, plus deemed knowledge. Better still, add the on-site community manager and the management company\\'s regional manager as knowledge parties. Restore all Form §8.1 reps (especially (d), (l), (o)), 12-month survival, Form §8.3 and the §2.2 carve-back. Delete the §6.4 waiver. At most, accept a narrow anti-sandbagging clause limited to matters actually known to named Buyer personnel before Closing. If a cap must be traded (IC approval), set it at a market-level percentage of price, well above $500,000, carved out for fraud, title, authority, FIRPTA, brokers, the certified rent roll and Seller indemnities, with a modest deductible.'],
['6','**Seller indemnification**\nForm Art. XV; Form §2.2(c)\nMkp: none','U: Article XV deleted in its entirety: Seller indemnity for rep and covenant breaches, pre-closing operation liabilities (pre-closing litigation, tenant and personal-injury claims), and environmental remediation for pre-closing conditions (no time limit). Only the narrow Assignment-of-Leases indemnity (Exhibit E) remains. Exhibit F (Assignment of Contracts) has no Assignor indemnity.','The IC memo (§§5.5, 6 Environmental Risk) relies on Seller bearing pre-closing litigation and remediation liabilities. Without Article XV, Buyer inherits pre-closing tort, tenant and vendor claims, and environmental conditions not caught by a Phase I.','**Reject; restore Article XV**, including the uncapped, unlimited-duration environmental indemnity. Fallback (IC consult): environmental indemnity survival of 5–7 years, plus pre-closing operation indemnity of 12–24 months outside any rep cap. Restore the mutual indemnities in Exhibits E and F.'],
['7','**Pre-closing operating covenants**\nForm §7.2(a)–(h)\nMkp §§7.2, 8.1(b)','T: entire covenant deleted: ordinary course, insurance, no new or modified leases or contracts without consent, no liens, maintenance, compliance, notices. Seller also inserted into condition 8.1(b) \"to the extent not deleted or modified hereby.\" Only a rep that Seller \"will maintain\" insurance (§6.1(j)) remains.','The 60-day gap (up to 90 days with extensions) is unprotected. Seller could sign below-market or long-term leases, amend or terminate the Little Oaks lease ($70,400/yr NNN, expires Dec. 31, 2027), sign long-term vendor contracts, defer maintenance, let occupancy slide, or encumber the Property. This contradicts the transmittal\\'s own assurance that Seller will continue to manage \"in the ordinary course.\" IC condition 1(e).','**Reject; restore Form §7.2 in full.** Point out that if Seller truly intends ordinary-course operation, the covenant costs it nothing. Possible concession: deemed consent if Buyer does not respond within 3 business days, and freedom to sign market-rate residential leases of 12 months or less (already in Form §7.2(c)). Delete the 8.1(b) qualifier.'],
['8','**Assignment**\nForm §14.1; Mkp §§1.1 (\"Buyer\"), 13.1, 16.6, Exh. C','T: no assignment without Seller consent \"in its sole and absolute discretion\"; non-consented assignment void. \"Buyer\" and the successors clause are limited to \"permitted assigns.\"','Fund III closes through a newly formed single-purpose entity (lender requirement; liability isolation). Seller would hold a veto it could use to renegotiate price or terms on the eve of Closing. IC condition 1(f).','**Reject; restore Form §14.1** (affiliate/SPE assignment without consent on 5 business days\\' notice; third-party assignment with consent not unreasonably withheld; Buyer not released). We can accept a written assumption by the assignee and Buyer remaining liable through Closing (already in our form).'],
],W, fills=['F8D7DA']*8)
EOF

doc.add_heading('Tier 2: High (insist on our form or a close variant)', level=2)
table(H,[
['9','**Title objections and cure**
Form §6.3
Mkp §4.3','T: Seller may "in its sole discretion" terminate the agreement if it is "unable or unwilling" to cure any objection. The cure period changes from 15 business days to 15 calendar days. U: deleted Seller\'s unconditional obligation to remove deeds of trust and other monetary liens and post-signing encumbrances; deleted the $50,000 cure commitment, Buyer\'s supplemental objections right, and the statement that Seller cannot terminate over title.','Seller could refuse to pay off its own mortgage and then terminate. Any Buyer objection becomes a free exit for Seller if the market rises or a better offer appears. Gap-period title matters have no objection mechanism.','**Reject the Seller termination right.** Restore Form §6.3(b)–(c): mandatory removal of monetary liens and Seller-created encumbrances; $50,000 cure effort; supplemental objections; Buyer-only election. Could accept 15 business days becoming 20 calendar days if timing requires.'],
['10','**Seller default remedies**
Form §13.1
Mkp §12.2','U: Buyer\'s remedies made "sole and exclusive." Cost reimbursement cut from $250,000 to **$50,000**. Specific performance must be "commenced within sixty (60) days after the scheduled Closing Date." Actual damages capped at the Purchase Price. Remedies no longer cumulative. T: §12.3 bars only Buyer from consequential damages.','IC §5.7 assumed $250,000 reimbursement and specific performance. Third-party reports, legal fees and lender deposits on a $57.2M deal can easily exceed $50,000. The 60-day suit window, combined with the new 30-day mediation precondition (Issue 17), can be used up before suit is possible.','Restore Form §13.1 (cure, cumulative remedies, $250,000 reimbursement, specific performance, actual damages). If Seller insists on a specific-performance window, accept no less than 90 days, tolled during any mediation, and add a willful-default damages remedy (e.g., Seller conveys to a third party).'],
['11','**Prorations and post-closing true-up**
Form §§11.1–11.2
Mkp §§10.1–10.2','T: accrual proration replaced with a **cash method**. Seller keeps "all rents . . . collected through and including the Closing Date"; expenses are allocated by when they are "due and payable." True-up deleted; prorations are "final." U: no credits for prepaid rents or security deposits (Form §11.1(f)–(g)); no tax re-proration; no Little Oaks NNN/CAM reconciliation.','With a Friday, Jan. 3, 2025 Closing, January rent (mostly collected Jan. 1–3) would stay with Seller. On T-12 EGI of $6,192,000 (about $516,000/month), Buyer would forgo up to about $480,000. Under our form, Seller is entitled only to Jan. 1–2 (about $33,000). Buyer would also pay pre-closing expenses billed after Closing, lose the security-deposit credit (Buyer becomes liable to tenants for deposits it never received), and lose tax and estimate true-ups.','**Reject.** Restore Form §11.1 (accrual as of 11:59 p.m. the day before Closing; credits for prepaid rents and security deposits) and §11.2 (90-day true-up; delinquent-rent waterfall). The only point in Seller\'s version that helps Buyer (Buyer keeps post-closing delinquent collections) is worth far less than what Buyer gives up.'],
['12','**Casualty and condemnation**
Form §§12.1–12.2
Mkp §§11.1–11.2','T: casualty termination threshold raised from $2,000,000 to **$5,000,000** (8.7% of price). (The "10% of value" test Seller deleted was in its retyped base, not our form.) ['19','**Seller due-diligence deliveries**\nForm §5.2\nMkp §5.2','U: list cut from 14 to 12 categories. Dropped: loss runs and 3-year claims history; pending tax appeals; environmental agency correspondence, asbestos, lead and mold reports; HOA or master association documents; personal property inventory; renovation contractor invoices, scopes and warranties. Added: certified rent roll; tenant correspondence.','These are the documents needed to underwrite insurance, environmental and renovation risk in a shortened period. Tie due-diligence expiry to complete delivery (Issue 4).'],
['20','**Closing deliveries and ancillary forms**\nForm §10.1, Exhs. C–E\nMkp §9.3, Exhs. D–F','U: dropped evidence of Seller\\'s authority (NC good-standing certificate; consent of Aldecott Family Holdings LP) and the gap indemnity. Bill of Sale (Exh. D) drops Seller\\'s warranty of good title to personal property free of liens. Assignment of Contracts (Exh. F) drops the mutual indemnity. Deed (Exh. C) recites $10 consideration and conveys to \"permitted assignee.\"','The title company will require authority and gap documents anyway. Without the personal-property title warranty, leased or financed equipment (for example, the package-locker system) could be subject to third-party claims.','Restore Form §10.1(f), (k) and the Exhibit C/D/E language. Add: termination of the existing management agreement and any non-assumed service contracts at Seller\\'s cost; Seller\\'s closing certificate re-making the reps (bring-down).'],

(Our form also has the LLC certify that it is **not** a disregarded entity.)','Briarwood\\'s sole member is Aldecott Family Holdings LP. A single-member LLC is a disregarded entity by default unless it elected corporate treatment. If so, the LP is the \"transferor\" and must give the certification. A defective certification exposes Buyer to withholding liability (up to 15% of amount realized).','Diligence: confirm Briarwood\\'s tax classification. If disregarded, the certification should be given by Aldecott Family Holdings LP, and our own Exhibit G should be conformed.'],
['22','**Legal description and personal property**\nForm Exh. A; Mkp Exhs. A–B','U: Seller replaced our legal description (Lot 1, Briarwood Commons Subdivision plat; rectangular metes and bounds of about 22.8 acres) with a different metes-and-bounds description following an unnamed tributary, based on a 2019 Carolina Land Surveying plat (Plat Book 312, Page 847). Exh. B lists the package lockers as \"Parcel Pending or similar\"; the IC memo describes Amazon Hub lockers.','The legal description defines what is conveyed and insured. A mismatch with the vesting deed, title commitment or new ALTA survey is a title risk. Equipment may be leased or vendor-owned.','Do not accept until Trident and our surveyor confirm against the vesting deed and the survey. Confirm which personal property is owned versus leased; schedule exclusions.'],
['23','**Notices**\nForm §16.1; Mkp §14.1','T: Seller suite 710 to 720; added Mr. Beatty\\'s email. U: Seller street 1400 to **1410** South Tryon (also in Exh. H). Email notice is effective only on \"confirmed receipt\" with a same-day courier copy (Form: on transmission, with follow-up within 1 business day).','The transmittal says Seller \"updated the notice addresses for both parties.\" The IC memo and transmittal use 195 Peachtree and the hawthorneandsable.com domain, so the markup may be correcting our form, but this must be confirmed rather than assumed. A \"confirmed receipt\" standard creates uncertainty for time-critical notices (due-diligence or financing termination at 5:00 p.m.).','Confirm all addresses directly with each party and firm IT (and correct our form if needed). Restore the Form email-delivery rule.'],
['24','**Buyer representations**\nForm §8.4; Mkp §6.3','U: added an OFAC/AML rep covering Buyer and all \"principals, partners, members, or affiliates.\" Buyer must be qualified in NC as of the Effective Date (Form: by Closing). Buyer\\'s financial-capacity rep was dropped, which helps Buyer.','A flat OFAC rep reaching every indirect investor in a $425M fund cannot be verified.','Accept the OFAC rep limited to Buyer and its direct owners, or to Buyer\\'s knowledge for indirect holders. Confirm Whitmore\\'s NC qualification or revert to \"by Closing.\"'],
['25','**Confidentiality**\nForm §16.10; Mkp §16.10','U: removed permitted disclosure to \"investors\" and the 2-year post-termination survival.','Fund III must report to the IC and limited partners.','Restore \"investors\" (and prospective co-investors and lenders) and the survival period.'],

['26','**Dates and business-day mechanics**\nForm §§1, 4.4, 5.2, 7.4, 16.11\nMkp §§7.3, 9.2, 16.8','U: deleted the Form §16.11 roll-forward to the next business day. Hard-coded dates do not work: the Jan. 18, 2025 extension date is a Saturday and Feb. 2, 2025 is a Sunday. The rent-roll date \"Dec. 29, 2024\" is a Sunday and is not 5 business days before Jan. 3 (that date is about Dec. 26, given the Dec. 25 and Jan. 1 holidays). Nov. 11, 2024 is Veterans Day, a bank holiday under the \"business day\" definition. **Our own form contains the same Dec. 29 and Nov. 11 errors.**','Seller signed nothing by Nov. 4 (its header is dated Nov. 8), so every hard-coded date tied to a Nov. 4 Effective Date (Nov. 7 deposit, Dec. 4 due diligence, Dec. 19 financing, Jan. 3 Closing) will be wrong at signing.','Restore the roll-forward. Express all deadlines as periods running from the actual Effective Date, with a closing-date schedule exhibit. Fix the Dec. 29 and Nov. 11 references in our own form.'],
['27','**\"Shall\" to \"will\" global change**\nThroughout (T)','T: about 140 instances changed. The new Seller-favorable provisions (Mkp §§3.3, 5.3, 6.2 cap, 6.4, 10.2, 12.3, 13.1) use \"shall.\"','Described as stylistic, but it creates inconsistent usage that invites argument that Seller\\'s \"will\" obligations are softer than Buyer\\'s \"shall\" obligations.','Reject the global change. Keep \"shall\" for all obligations.'],
['28','**Numbering, cross-references, artifacts**','Duplicate \"Section 7.2\" (operating covenants heading and renumbered estoppel). §9.3(g)/(k) cross-references re-pointed. Headings contain bracketed \"[DELETED]/[ADDED]\" text. Stray deleted \"shall\" runs at the end of §7.1. §3.3 refers to conditions in \"Section 8.1\"; §1.1 refers to \"Article 13.\"','A clean conformed document will be needed. Errors can change meaning (for example, which section is \"Section 7.2\").','Conform at our next turn on our own form.'],
['29','**Deposit wiring protocol**\n(transmittal)','Mr. Beatty says he will circulate Trident wiring instructions \"under separate cover.\"','Wire instructions sent by a party\\'s counsel by email are a known wire-fraud vector. A $750,000 deposit is a meaningful target.','Obtain instructions only from Trident (Maria Fontaine) and verify by phone to a known number before funding. Mkp §3.1 language (account designated by the Escrow Officer) is acceptable.'],
],W, fills=['E2EFDA']*4)

**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL \| ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION \| ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

**MEMORANDUM**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **TO:**                             Margaret Chen, Partner; for onward discussion with Whitmore Capital Partners LLC (Acquisitions Team; David Whitmore and Rebecca Tanaka, Investment Committee)
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **FROM:**                           Hawthorne & Sable LLP real estate deal team

  **CC:**                             Kyle Prater, Senior Associate

  **DATE:**                           November 2024 (prepared on receipt of Seller\'s markup transmitted November 1, 2024)

  **RE:**                             The Ellington at Briarwood (4700 Briarwood Commons Drive, Charlotte, NC 28270): prioritized issues list on Seller\'s (Ridgeline Beatty LLP) markup of Buyer\'s form Purchase and Sale Agreement circulated October 21, 2024
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# I. Bottom Line

The transmittal describes the markup as \"balanced, market-standard\" with \"clean-up and stylistic edits\" and some \"refined\" representations. It is not. Read against our October 21 form and the October 28, 2024 IC memorandum, the markup reverses nearly every core risk-allocation term the Investment Committee approved. It turns a refundable, financing-protected deposit into an uncapped, all-cash closing obligation. It also strips away most of Buyer\'s post-closing recourse and pre-closing protections. We recommend that Whitmore **not sign** on these terms, and that we **not** treat November 4, 2024 as a realistic Effective Date.

**The ten points that matter most:**

> **1. Financing contingency deleted (tracked).** The markup goes further than deleting it: Buyer must close \"regardless of whether Buyer has obtained a loan commitment.\" The IC memo calls the contingency \"non-negotiable\" (§5.3). About 65% of the price (7,180,000) is debt-funded, and Fund III has no authority to close all-cash.
>
> **2. Earnest Money goes hard at the end of due diligence for any reason other than Seller default (tracked).** Failure of financing \"shall not entitle Buyer to a refund.\" This is the exact change the IC memo says would \"materially alter the risk profile\" (§5.1).
>
> **3. Buyer\'s exposure on default becomes uncapped (tracked).** The ,500,000 deposit becomes a \"minimum, and not a maximum\" measure of damages. Seller adds specific performance and actual and consequential damages, and the consequential-damages waiver now runs only in Seller\'s favor. Combined with items 1 and 2, Fund III could be sued to compel an all-cash close of 7.2 million.
>
> **4. Due Diligence Period cut from 30 to 21 days (tracked).** It would expire Monday, November 25, 2024 (Thanksgiving week), and the 50,000 Additional Deposit would be accelerated to that date.
>
> **5. Seller\'s representations are close to illusory (tracked and untracked).** The knowledge standard becomes \"actual knowledge . . . without any duty of investigation or inquiry\" of a manager whom Seller\'s counsel describes as having \"limited direct involvement.\" Survival drops from 12 months to 3 months. There is a new 00,000 cap (0.87% of price), a waiver of anything \"that could have been discovered\" in diligence, and several representations have been deleted without tracking.
>
> **6. Seller indemnification article (Form Article XV) deleted entirely, without tracking.** This removes the pre-closing liability indemnity and the environmental remediation indemnity, which had no time limit.
>
> **7. All pre-closing operating covenants deleted (Form §7.2; tracked).** This happens over a 60-to-90-day gap period. A new condition qualifier (\"to the extent not deleted or modified hereby\") makes the closing condition toothless.
>
> **8. Assignment barred without Seller\'s consent \"in its sole and absolute discretion\" (tracked).** That blocks the planned assignment to a single-purpose entity that Palisade National Bank and Fund III\'s structuring require.
>
> **9. Title: Seller gets a walk right (tracked) and no longer has to pay off its own mortgage liens (untracked).** In a rising market, this gives Seller a free option to terminate.
>
> **10. The markup is not a true redline of our form.** Its \"original\" text is a different, retyped base document, so many substantive changes appear nowhere as tracked changes. The revision metadata is generic (author \"Author\", dated January 1, 2024). The document header is dated November 8, 2024, which conflicts with the November 1 email. We must work from our own comparison against the October 21 form (Section II) and should ask Ridgeline Beatty for a true comparison.

**IC authority.** At least eight IC conditions are directly affected (see Section III). These include the four that IC §8 expressly says require supplemental authorization: the financing contingency, deposit refundability, survival and scope of representations, and assignment. The Acquisitions Team cannot accept any of these as drafted, or any meaningful compromise on them, without returning to the IC first.

**Recommended posture.** Reject the Tier 1 items outright and return our form with targeted concessions on lower-priority points (Section VII). Ask Seller\'s counsel to re-run the comparison against the October 21 form before the next turn. Reset the Effective Date and every hard-coded date to the actual signing date.

# II. Threshold Problem: The Markup Is Not a Redline of Our Form

The document has 158 tracked insertions and 157 tracked deletions. But the deleted (\"original\") text is **not** our October 21 form. Seller\'s counsel produced a retyped agreement with a different structure (16 articles renumbered; for example, Assignment is Article 13 instead of XIV, and Default is Article 12 instead of XIII). They then tracked changes against that new base. The result is that many substantive departures from our form appear as clean, untracked text. Specifically:

- **Provisions dropped without any tracked deletion:** Form §2.2 (the paragraph protecting representations, covenants and indemnities from the as-is clause), §3.3(b)--(c) (refund events after due diligence and the failure-to-deposit mechanics), §4.3 (closing costs), §6.3(b) (mandatory cure of monetary liens, the 0,000 cure commitment, and supplemental objections), §8.3 (no liability cap), the §9.2 closing paragraph (Buyer\'s right to terminate with a refund when a condition fails), the §9.2(f)--(g) conditions (no new title matters; estoppel), Article XV (indemnification in full), §16.10 survival and investor disclosure, and the §16.11 business-day roll-forward.

- **Terms changed without tracking:** Seller-default remedies (cost reimbursement cut from 50,000 to 0,000; remedies made \"sole and exclusive\"; a 60-day deadline to sue for specific performance; damages capped). Also: deletion of the cure period for Buyer default, deletion of the inspection-indemnity carve-out for \"mere discovery of pre-existing conditions,\" estoppel timing (10 to 5 business days), the Extension Fee payee and refund, arbitration replaced by litigation with a jury waiver, a new Buyer OFAC representation, the Exhibit A legal description, Bill of Sale title warranty, notice addresses (Seller 1400 to 1410 South Tryon; Hawthorne 191 to 195 Peachtree and a new email domain), and several Seller representations narrowed or deleted (see Issue 5).

- **Unreliable metadata:** every revision carries the generic author \"Author\" and the date January 1, 2024. The header reads \"Seller\'s Counsel Markup . . . November 8, 2024,\" while the transmittal email is dated November 1, 2024 (and both are after or near the targeted November 4 Effective Date and November 7 Initial Deposit date).

input.message:
I've written the prioritized issues memo, `psa-markup-issues-memo.docx`. It passes the docx skill's validator, reads back correctly with parse-doc, and converts to a 19-page PDF. I read all four documents in full. I also pulled the tracked changes straight from the redline's XML and checked them clause by clause against our October 21 form and the IC memo.

**The main finding:** the seller's "redline" isn't marked against our form. Ridgeline Beatty retyped the agreement into a different structure and tracked changes against that new text, so many substantive changes show up as clean, untracked text. The revision metadata is generic (author "Author", dated 1/1/2024). The markup header is dated Nov 8, 2024, but the transmittal email is dated Nov 1. The memo recommends we respond only against our own form and ask for a true comparison.

**How the memo is organized:**
- **Bottom line:** the ten points that matter most and a recommended posture. Don't sign as drafted, and drop Nov 4 as the Effective Date.
- **IC authority check:** a table showing each IC approval condition the markup breaches.
- **Issues list:** 29 issues in four tiers. Each row gives the form and markup sections, whether the change was tracked or untracked, what Seller did, why it matters, and our recommended response.

**Tier 1 (reject; IC authorization needed to concede):**
1. Financing contingency deleted, and Buyer must close without financing.
2. The full $1.5M deposit goes hard when due diligence ends.
3. The liquidated-damages cap is gone: the deposit becomes a "minimum", and Seller can seek specific performance and consequential damages.
4. Due diligence cut from 30 to 21 days, ending Nov 25, 2024.
5. Seller's reps are gutted:
   - knowledge limited to Mr. Aldecott's actual knowledge, with no duty of inquiry;
   - survival cut to 3 months, with a new $500K cap;
   - Buyer waives anything that "could have been discovered" in diligence;
   - the renovation rep and the no-options/ROFR rep were deleted without tracking.
6. The Seller indemnity article (Article XV) was deleted without tracking.
7. All pre-closing operating covenants were deleted.
8. Assignment now needs Seller's consent in its sole discretion, which blocks the planned assignment to a single-purpose entity.

**Tier 2 to 4 highlights:**
- Title: Seller gets a walk right and no longer has to pay off its own liens.
- Seller-default cost reimbursement cut from $250K to $50K, without tracking.
- Prorations move to a cash basis with no true-up. Seller could keep up to about $480K of January rent.
- Casualty termination threshold raised from $2M to $5M.
- The Little Oaks estoppel is no longer a closing condition.
- The closing-cost allocation is gone, including the NC excise tax of about $114,400.
- Mediation now delays any specific-performance suit.
- FIRPTA: Briarwood is likely a disregarded entity, so the certification may need to come from Aldecott Family Holdings LP.
- The legal description was replaced with a different one.
- Notice addresses and email domains changed, some untracked. Confirm them rather than assume either version is right.
- Hard-coded dates need fixing: Jan 18 and Feb 2, 2025 fall on a weekend, and Dec 29, 2024 is a Sunday. Our own form has the Dec 29 and Nov 11 errors too.
- Wire instructions should come only from Trident and be confirmed by phone.

The memo closes with:
- a combined-exposure timeline under the markup;
- a table setting the transmittal's descriptions against what the markup actually does;
- a three-tier negotiating position (reject / concessions we can offer / fallbacks only with IC approval);
- next steps;
- a section concordance between our form and the markup.

The dollar figures (January rent, excise tax) are estimates from the IC memo's trailing-12-month numbers. The memo says it doesn't reflect any title commitment, survey, lease or third-party report.

Files are in /workspace/output:
- psa-markup-issues-memo.docx
